description: The death cap is a deadly poisonous ectomycorrhizal mushroom responsible for the majority of fatal mushroom poisonings worldwide. It typically produces a greenish to yellowish cap, white free gills, a white skirt-like ring, and a membranous sac-like volva at the base, with a white spore print. Its lethal amatoxins cause severe liver and kidney failure, often after a deceptive symptom-free latency period.
edibilityNotes: Contains amatoxins (chiefly alpha-amanitin) that are not destroyed by cooking, drying, or freezing. As little as half a cap can be fatal to an adult. Symptoms typically begin 6-12 hours after ingestion (gastrointestinal phase), followed by a deceptive period of apparent recovery, then progressive liver and kidney failure. Seek emergency medical care immediately on any suspicion of ingestion. Never eat.
distribution: Native to Europe, it has spread widely via introduced trees and now occurs across North America, North Africa, Australia, New Zealand, and parts of Asia and South America.

dangerousLookalikes.name: Volvariella volvacea (paddy-straw mushroom)
dangerousLookalikes.note: An edible species cultivated in Asia and a recurring cause of fatal confusion. Volvariella has a PINK spore print and pink mature gills, and lacks a ring on the stem; the death cap has a white spore print, white gills, and a distinct skirt-like ring. Both have a volva, so spore color and the ring are the decisive features.

dangerousLookalikes.name: Amanita citrina (false death cap)
dangerousLookalikes.note: Pale lemon-yellow, with a rounded marginate (not sac-like) volval bulb and a raw-potato smell; considered inedible but not deadly. Distinguished by the abrupt bulb versus the death cap's loose membranous sac-like volva.

dangerousLookalikes.name: Agaricus species (edible field/button mushrooms)
dangerousLookalikes.note: Young button-stage death caps are mistaken for Agaricus buttons. Agaricus have pink then chocolate-brown gills and a brown spore print and never have a volva; always cut and excavate the base and check for the sac-like volva, which Agaricus lacks.

dangerousLookalikes.name: Edible white-spored Amanita and Lepiota species
dangerousLookalikes.note: All-white forms (and the white var. alba) resemble other pale gilled mushrooms. Always excavate the full stem base to reveal the volva, and avoid any white-gilled, white-spored, volva-bearing, ringed Amanita.
